result.content: {"answer_sections": [{"text": "The chronicle Târîh-i Râşid notes that Burunsuz, a pirate nicknamed 'Burunsuz,' targeted only Muslim-Turkish trade ships.", "claim_ids": ["c-1e0f976477238be2f174", "c-9fa9ce46cce4e38234f4"]}, {"text": "Astypalaia served as a safe anchorage for corsairs, offering provisions and shelter.", "claim_ids": ["c-4c1222f0df72fb1ae71a"]}, {"text": "Dieudé left Crete in 1686, settling in Milos and collaborating with Ottoman adversaries.", "claim_ids": ["c-85b6d86ecf971dd0f67d"]}, {"text": "Corsairs operated from Oran, Tlemcen, Bizerta, Sfax, Susa, Monastir, Jerbah, and Tripoli.", "claim_ids": ["c-e5bbc3264384075aa4f5", "c-b76cbd68d372c2f26c6e", "c-9152ff94afa4973daa9e"]}], "unknowns": ["Verification status of sources remains pending.", "Unclear if all listed locations were actual pirate bases or merely points of operation.", "Ambiguity in the exact role of certain locations like Bizerta and Sfax in pirate activities."], "limitations": ["Some sources are secondary and unverified.", "Dates and specific usage types are not fully resolved in all claims.", "Lack of direct evidence on the exact nature of certain locations' involvement in piracy."]}
